items.title: Fourth Press Briefing on Bhote Koshi Flood
items.summary: Search teams have recovered 1010 bodies, with around 4000 people still unaccounted for. More than 11800 people have been rescued so far.
items.citation: Nepal Ministry of Foreign Affairs — Fourth Press Briefing on Bhote Koshi Flood

items.title: Fifth Press Briefing on Bhote Koshi Floods
items.summary: Rescue teams from India, China, and South Korea are working with Nepali teams to clear tunnels and search the affected areas. So far 11,993 people have been rescued while around 3,900 remain missing and 1,114 bodies have been recovered.
items.citation: Nepal Ministry of Foreign Affairs — Fifth Press Briefing on Bhote Koshi Floods

items.title: Diplomatic Briefing by Hon. Minister for Foreign Affairs Mr Shisir Khanal on the Bhote Koshi Floods
items.summary: A massive flood hit the Bhote Koshi on August 26 and tore through Rasuwa and four other districts. So far 1,204 bodies have been recovered, around 4,200 people remain missing, and nearly 12,000 have been rescued.
items.citation: Nepal Ministry of Foreign Affairs — Diplomatic Briefing by Hon. Minister for Foreign Affairs Mr Shisir Khanal on the Bhote Koshi Floods

items.title: Sixth Press Briefing on Bhote Koshi Floods
items.summary: Search teams from Nepal and other countries are still looking for around 4,200 people missing after the floods. Over 11,000 people have been rescued so far, and work continues with international help on tunnels and DNA checks.
items.citation: Nepal Ministry of Foreign Affairs — Sixth Press Briefing on Bhote Koshi Floods

items.title: Foreign nationals — missing, rescued, or contacted (NDRRMA, 1 Sep)
items.summary: There's an update on foreign nationals missing, rescued, or contacted after the Bhote Koshi flood in Rasuwa. It points to the tourism department's list and the situation report from August 30.
items.citation: NDRRMA Nepal — X post (1 September 2026)

items.title: Embassy of India — identification of mortal remains (1 Sep 2026)
items.summary: The Indian Embassy in Kathmandu has guidance for families on identifying and collecting remains after the Nepal floods. Relatives can check photos and descriptions via Nepal Police or contact them for DNA matching and handover details.
items.citation: Embassy of India, Kathmandu — Press Release (1 September 2026)

items.title: Press Briefing by the Spokesperson on Bhote Koshi Flood
items.summary: Rescue teams have pulled more than 10,000 people out of the flood-hit areas, including over 323 foreign nationals. So far 903 bodies have been recovered, around 4,200 people are still unaccounted for, and about 590 foreigners from 39 countries remain missing.
items.citation: Nepal Ministry of Foreign Affairs — Press Briefing by the Spokesperson on Bhote Koshi Flood

items.title: Nepal Police — DNA profiling for unidentified remains
items.summary: Families with relatives missing from the Rasuwa and Bhote Koshi floods can help identify recovered bodies by giving DNA samples. In Nepal, first-degree relatives can provide a blood sample and photos at the Nepal Police Hospital or a district police office; those abroad should send results from an authorised lab.
items.citation: Nepal Police HQ — Information on DNA Profiling for unidentified Dead Bodies (31 Aug)

items.title: NDRRMA — Bhotekoshi water level rising again (31 Aug)
items.summary: The Bhotekoshi River's water level is rising again. People in Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading, Chitwan and nearby areas should stay careful.
items.citation: NDRRMA Nepal — public warning via official channels

items.title: Press Briefing Note by Foreign Secretary on Bhote Koshi Flood (Sunday, 2:00 PM, 30 August 2026)
items.summary: Search teams have recovered 734 bodies after the Bhote Koshi floods, while about 2,500 people remain unaccounted for. More than 8,000 people have been rescued so far, including over 260 foreign nationals.
items.citation: Nepal Ministry of Foreign Affairs — Press Briefing Note by Foreign Secretary on Bhote Koshi Flood (Sunday, 2:00 PM, 30 August 2026)

items.title: Press Briefing Note by Hon. Minister for Foreign Affairs on Bhote Koshi Flood
items.summary: Flash floods struck the Bhote Koshi River on 26 August, and teams have recovered 626 bodies while about 2400 people are still missing. Over 4450 people have been rescued so far, including more than 187 foreign nationals, with searches continuing in the affected areas.
items.citation: Nepal Ministry of Foreign Affairs — Press Briefing Note by Hon. Minister for Foreign Affairs on Bhote Koshi Flood

items.title: Latest Updates on Flash Floods- 28 August 2026
items.summary: Flash floods hit Nepal's Bhote Koshi River on 26 August, destroying homes, roads, bridges and other infrastructure while leaving many people missing. Rescue teams have recovered 538 bodies so far, with 511 of 632 reported missing still unaccounted for.
items.citation: Nepal Ministry of Foreign Affairs — Latest Updates on Flash Floods- 28 August 2026

items.title: FOCUS | Rescue operations at mudslide-hit border port in SW China's Xizang
items.summary: Rescue teams reached the mudslide area at Gyirong Port on Thursday morning. Three people have been confirmed dead and 558 remain missing after the slide hit the day before.
items.citation: Xinhua (Gyirong / Tibet side) — FOCUS | Rescue operations at mudslide-hit border port in SW China's Xizang

items.title: Latest Updates on Flash Floods-27 August 2026
items.summary: Flash floods hit Nepal’s Bhote Koshi River area on 26 August. So far 359 bodies have been recovered and 596 people from 33 countries are still missing.
items.citation: Nepal Ministry of Foreign Affairs — Latest Updates on Flash Floods-27 August 2026

items.title: NOTICE: Emergency Control Room (ECR) for Assistance regarding Foreign Nationals Affected by the Bhote Koshi Flash Flood
items.summary:
Nepal’s foreign ministry has set up an emergency room to help with foreign nationals missing or affected by the Rasuwa floods.
Call or message +977-9744441227 or +977-9744441228 between 7am and 10pm.
items.citation: Nepal Ministry of Foreign Affairs — NOTICE: Emergency Control Room (ECR) for Assistance regarding Foreign Nationals Affected by the Bhote Koshi Flash Flood

items.title: Special Control Room in MEA for Nepal Floods Situation
items.summary: India’s external affairs ministry has opened a 24-hour control room in Delhi for the Nepal floods. Families can reach it at +91 11 2308 8718, +91 11 2308 8719 or +91 11 2301 2113.
items.citation: MEA press release — Special Control Room in MEA for Nepal Floods Situation

items.title: Latest Updates on Flash Floods- 26 August 2026
items.summary: Flash floods hit Nepal this morning, causing deaths and damage to homes, roads, bridges and other infrastructure. So far 72 bodies have been recovered and 403 people are reported missing.
items.citation: Nepal Ministry of Foreign Affairs — Latest Updates on Flash Floods- 26 August 2026
